title: A DR1 user who cannot find their commercial transporter on the list can add one; a frontend user can only pick from the two the service hands them, and has no way to record a commercial transporter that is not on that list.

finding.frontend: Choosing Commercial leads to `/transporters/select`, which renders the whole commercial list as radios and validates that the answer is one of the ids it rendered (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:23-29). There is no add link, no manual-entry fallback and no free-text field. Two records exist. If the transporter moving the animals is not one of those two, the notification cannot say who is moving the animals — the journey has no other route through. The private branch does allow free entry, so the only way out today is to misdescribe a commercial transporter as a private one.
finding.prototype: DR1's list page has an "Add a transporter" button, and choosing Commercial on the type page reaches `/transporter/add-commercial`, a full create form (app/views/partials/transporter-add-commercial-fields.html). It collects: Transporter authorisation number; Name or organisation name; an address, either through a "Search for an address" lookup or manual entry of Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code and Country; and, under an "Enter contact details" heading, Email address and Phone number. The page also repeats the transporter-authorisation guidance in an Important panel so a user filling the form can check the authorisation rules while they do it. Saving adds the transporter to the list and returns the user to it.
finding.difference: Add an add-commercial-transporter page reachable from the transporter list. The whole field set above is new work in the frontend — in particular the transporter authorisation number, which the frontend never collects on either transporter branch. Two decisions sit inside it and both need settling before the page can be built: whether an added commercial transporter is stored on the notification or in a register other notifications can reuse, and whether DR1's Northern-Ireland-only restriction on commercial transporters is a real policy the form must enforce.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any route in the frontend that records a commercial transporter not present in the commercial-transporter list — an add link, a manual-entry reveal, or a free-text name field on `/transporters/select`.

relatedTo.why: The add form hangs off the Add a transporter button on the list page
DR1 fixes this form's Country to Northern Ireland; the restriction has to be settled before the form is built
